title: manifestCycle() shares the backtick-inclusive leading character class that legacyReadyForCheck()/legacyStatusPresent() just had to have removed for the identical false-positive class -- a latent defect, not yet live
evidence: handshake-field-reader (checker, cycle 0). The unit's own docstring (scripts/lib/dispatch-state.mjs, above legacyReadyForCheck) explains the bug it fixed: the old regex's leading class `[\s\-*#>|`]*` let a backtick-opened inline-code span (e.g. a sentence quoting `` `## Status: ready-for-check` `` as documentation prose) satisfy `^` and be misread as a real field declaration, confirmed live against delivery-gate-manifest-blindness.md and mc-hooks-bolded-status.md (both false disagreements before the fix, 0 after). manifestCycle() (scripts/lib/dispatch-state.mjs:42-45) reads `/^[\s\-*#>|`]*Fix cycle:\s*(\d+)/m` against the RAW text with no stripQuoted()-style pre-pass -- the exact same vulnerable shape, confirmed by direct read; the unit's manifest explicitly leaves it untouched as out of its authorized scope (D-043 item 3 covers only the manifest-state/ready-for-check reading). Live-scanned the full 162-manifest corpus for a backtick-quoted 'Fix cycle' mention: 10 files carry one (delivery-gate-manifest-blindness.md, delivery-gate-stamp-adoption.md, eval-baseline-control.md, mc-hooks-bolded-status.md, search-prefilter-bypass-pin.md, search-prefilter-coverage.md, search-prefilter.md, search-store-injectable-handle.md, search-store-tenant-assertion.md, web-ask-page.md). In every one of the 10, the quoted mention happens to sit AFTER the file's own real `**Fix cycle:** N` field (which `manifestCycle()`'s unanchored-position `.exec()` therefore finds first), so `manifestCycle()`'s returned value matches the true field in all 10 today -- 0 live misreads, confirmed by direct comparison. This is a coincidence of document ordering, not a property of the regex: a manifest that quotes a DIFFERENT cycle number in a backtick span BEFORE its own real Fix cycle field (plausible in any manifest documenting this exact bug class, which several of these 10 already do) would have that quoted number read as the file's fix cycle instead of the true one.
reproduction: Constructed fixture (matching the live corpus's own shape, where the quoting sentence opens the line -- confirmed this is required for the match, an earlier draft of this repro with the span mid-line correctly did NOT trigger it): text = '`Fix cycle: 9`, an example of the bug class.\n\n**Fix cycle:** 1 of max 3'; manifestCycle(text) -> 9, not 1. Verified live via node -e against scripts/lib/dispatch-state.mjs.
fix_direction: Same fix already applied two functions over: drop the backtick from manifestCycle()'s leading character class, or (more robust, matching verdictCycle()'s own approach) route it through stripQuoted() before matching. Out of scope for handshake-field-reader (D-043 item 3 authorizes only the ready-for-check/pending reading); needs its own unit or a follow-on authorized change since manifestCycle() backs a fix-cycle count used across the handshake contract.

title: D-049 misattributes D-043 item 3's completion to `ledger-shard-union-reader`, a unit that (per its own checker-corrected manifest) never touched the handshake canonical field
evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md D-049 (line ~931-933): 'D-043 remains ACTIVE and correct for item 3 (.claude/hooks/mc-sessionstart.ps1, genuinely repo-local, built and PASSed as `ledger-shard-union-reader`).' Read qa/manifests/ledger-shard-union-reader.md directly: its own 'Issues addressed' line, corrected at close-out per the checker's ISS-353, reads 'ISS-129 -- and ISS-129 only', with an explicit boxed note that the manifest ORIGINALLY also claimed ISS-350 (reproduction 2) and that 'the checker diffed the unit and showed neither is touched by it: the change is two hunks confined to the $LEDGER/$n lines'. That unit was authorized by D-041 (the ledger-union glob fix), not D-043, and is a different seam entirely (multi-shard issues.jsonl union counting vs. the canonical **Handshake status:** field this current unit, handshake-field-reader, is the first to teach either reader to read). D-049's 'built and PASSed as' claim is therefore false on the same corpus D-049 itself cites, and on the exact axis (an id/unit misattribution) this repo's own D-015/D-019/ISS-353/ISS-364 history keeps finding. It does NOT undermine handshake-field-reader's own authorization -- D-043 item 3's Approved-by/Changes-authorized text names the file and change directly and is unaffected by which unit (if any) D-049 believed had already built it -- but it is a live inaccuracy in an ACTIVE decisions-log entry that a future reader could use to wrongly conclude item 3's reader-side work was already done.
reproduction: Read docs/DECISIONS.md D-049's item-3 sentence, then read qa/manifests/ledger-shard-union-reader.md's 'Issues addressed' line and its close-out correction box.

grep -c 'HANDSHAKE_VOCAB\|canonicalHandshakeStatus' against the commit ledger-shard-union-reader actually shipped (36909f1) -- 0; those symbols first appear in handshake-field-reader's own commit 1f263e0.
fix_direction: A correcting DECISIONS entry (or an amendment note against D-049, per this repo's append-only/never-edit convention) stating item 3's reader-side work was actually delivered by handshake-field-reader, not ledger-shard-union-reader. Low severity: no authorization or scope depends on the mislabeled clause, so nothing needs to be undone -- only the record corrected for the next reader.
